messages.subject: Re: Gsoc projects 2017
messages.body_plain:
Project ideas go here:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki

specifically:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects

If a student wants to propose a project, they should certainly feel free
to propose on on the project table.

To enhance chances for success of such a student-driven project, I would
strongly suggest choosing an existing package in the area of the
proposal and contacting the maintainer or development team for that
package with your proto-proposal. Proposals are more likely to be
accepted if they have had a fair amount of work done on them prior to
GSoC, often including code, but certainly showing a great deal of
thought and planning, especially when the mentors are also new to GSoC.

Regards,

Brian

--

messages.subject: Re: Wrapping up R's GSoC 2016 projects
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

my name Balázs Dukai and I participated as a student in the GSoC 2016. With my mentors Mathieu Basille, David Buckling and Clément Calenge we've been working a package called 'rpostgisLT'. This package provides the integration of R and PostGIS for managing movement trajectories. The focus is on streamlining the workflow for biologists to store and process animal trajectories in PostGIS and analyze these in R, thus utilizing the strengths of both software. Therefore the main outcome of GSoC 2016 is the previously named R package which simplifies the processing of location datasets into trajectories in PostGIS and provide full integration with the R package adehabitatlt data type ltraj.

Although we didn't get to a point with the package to publish it on CRAN, there is not much left in order to do so and the package is already operational. You can check it out and follow the development at: https://github.com/mablab/rpostgisLT

Hereby I also invite you to read my personal summary of the project: https://github.com/mablab/rpostgisLT/wiki/GSoC-2016

Balázs

> have coded some technical and fundamental indicators in c++ and collaborated
> it with RCPP with R fro analysis.

Indicators are a very minor component of a back testing platform.  The
complexity and time consuming portion lies in the state machine.

> Here is my code for 1 indicators and github link for rest of my indicators
> (35 indicators-code)
> 1.For technical indicators.
>  https://github.com/AshwinAgrawal16/Technical-Indicators-in-RCPP-and-R
>

Most of the technical indicators in your repo are already in the TTR
package.  Those that are not could easily be written using the
indicators in TTR.

Using OpenMP for these calculations is overkill, because indicator
calculation is not often a bottleneck, and there is potential for
issues related to OpenMP.  A cursory look at your code suggests most
of your loops in your functions could be consolidated into a single
pass.

> 2.For fundamental indicators
> https://github.com/AshwinAgrawal16/Fundamental-Indicators-And-Ratios
>

Writing simple calculations for fundamental data in C++ is
unnecessarily complex.

> //TWIGGS MONEY FLOW FORMULA
>
<snip>

>
> I am currently working on developing some new indicators and developed quite
> a few (which are not present in link-confidential) and in process of coding
> more indicators.

Again, most of these are probably already in TTR, so it's not clear
what your proposal adds to the existing set of packages.

On Wed, Sep 28, 2016 at 3:23 AM,  <ashwin.agr...@itbhu.ac.in> wrote:

> The description of the operators are as follows and then some simple filter
> and reversion strategies which could be build using these operators and
> market data.
> (i will code them in near future)
>
As I said in my previous response:

1) Most of the operators/indicators you propose already exist.  There
is no clear benefit to rewriting them.  Most of your examples below
could use the existing functions.

2) Indicators are a very minor component of a back testing platform.
The complexity and time consuming portion lies in the state machine.
Your proposed state machine (TradeWhen) seems extremely simple, and
there are already packages that perform this simple type of state
machine (e.g., https://github.com/danielkrizian/strategery,
https://github.com/systematicinvestor/SIT).

> Rank(x)   =Rank the values of x among all instruments, and the return values
> are float numbers equally distributed between 0.0 and 1.0
>
> StdDev(x, n) =Standard deviation of the values in vector x for the past n
> days.
>
> Sum(x, n)= Sum of the values in vector x for the past n days.
>
> Correlation(x, y, n)=  Correlation of the values in vectors x and y for the
> past n days.
>
> Covariance(x, y, n)  =Covariance of the values in vectors x and y for the
> past n days.
>
> Count_Nans_Number(x, n)=Number of nan (Not-a-Number) values in vector x for
> the past n days.
>
> Delay(x, n)-=Value of x at n days ago.
>
> Delta(x, n)-=x[date] - x[date - n].
>
> Decay_Simple_linear(x, n)
>
>
> Decay_Simple_linear(x, n) = (x[date] * n + x[date - 1] * (n - 1) + ..... +
> x[date – n - 1]) / (n + (n - 1) + … + 1)
>
> Ts_Rank(x, n)=Rank the values of x of the same instrument over the past n
> days, then return the rank of the current value. The rank value is between
> 0.0 ~ 1.0
>
> GroupRank(group, x)= Returns the rank of each instrument within a group,
> which can be any matrix
>
> SignedPower(x, e)=Sign(x) * (Abs(x)^e)
>
> Ts_Skewness(x, n)=Compute the skewness of x on the last n days
>
> Ts_Kurtosis(x, n)=Compute the kurtosis of x on the last n days.
>
> Ts_Moment(x, k, n)=Compute the kth central moment of x on the last n days
>
> Ts_Regression(y, x, window, lag, retval)=y[t] = a + b * x[t-lag] for t in
> (Today - window, Today)
>
> TradeWhen(x, y, z)=TradeWhen(triggerTradeExp, alphaExp, triggerExitExp).
>
> ArgMax(x, n)=Returns the relative index of the max value in the time series
> x for the past n days.
>
> Ts_mean(x, n)=Calculates mean of the variable in last n days
>
> Ts_max(x, n)=Time series max of the value
>
> THESE ALL BELOW CODES PRODUCES VECTOR OF STOCK WEIGHTS FOR DIFFERENT GROUP
> OF STOCKS
> THESE CAN EASILY BE COMBINED WITH PERFORMANCE ANALYTICS PACKAGE FOR SHARPE
> ,TURNOVER ,DRAWDOWN, RETURNS etc(Pnl also)
> THESE OPERATORS WILL EASE THE WORK FOR BUILDING STRATEGIES AND CAN EASILY BE
> EVALUATED USING PA PACKAGE IN R
> MANY MORE OPERATORS ARE THERE.(GUI CAN ALSO BE BUILD)
>
> //below codes i used Fibonacci retracements and Elliot Wave Theory to find
> the time period(n) and indicators for the reversion strategies.
> 1.Here using volume as the filter condition and correlation between volume
> and weighted volume price(vwap) as simple reversion strategy
>
> x=volume>decay_linear(volume,233);
> y=(-1 * ts_max(rank(correlation(rank(volume), rank(vwap), 5)), 5));
> TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
>
>
> 2.Here using volume as filter condition and stochastic oscillator as the
> base

>
>

> 3.Using sentimental value and volume as filter condition and mean-reversion
> strategy.
>
>
> x=snt_social_value>sum(snt_social_value,14)/14 && volume>sum(volume,14)/14;
> adv30=delay(sum(volume,30)/30,1);
> y=-2*rank(log(close/open))+2*(( (((-1 * rank((open - delay(high, 1)))) *
> rank((open - delay(close, 1)))) * rank((open-delay(low, 1)))))+ (-1 *
> Ts_Rank(rank(low), 5)))+(rank(correlation(vwap, volume, 4)) <

> 12)));
> TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
>
> 4.Earnings per share and volume as filter condition and close-vwap

>
>
> x=volume>sum(volume,14)/14 && eps>sum(eps,14)/14;

>
> 5.Simple reversion with no filter

messages.body_plain:
So can you yourself suggest some area in finance in R programming where i can work for the project.

On Wednesday, September 28, 2016 at 9:47:14 PM UTC+5:30, Joshua Ulrich wrote:
> Please don't start a new thread (by changing the email subject) in
> order to continue a conversation. This makes it difficult to follow
> the discussion for people who use threaded email readers.
>
> On Wed, Sep 28, 2016 at 3:23 AM,  <ashwin.agr...@itbhu.ac.in> wrote:
> > I will elaborate my idea(and why i coded the indicators),my plan is to build
> > certain operators which will help in building trading strategies with R
> > ,without using long lines of code and just using the inbuild operators.
> > The description of the operators are as follows and then some simple filter
> > and reversion strategies which could be build using these operators and
> > market data.
> > (i will code them in near future)
> >
> As I said in my previous response:
>
> 1) Most of the operators/indicators you propose already exist.  There
> is no clear benefit to rewriting them.  Most of your examples below
> could use the existing functions.
>
> 2) Indicators are a very minor component of a back testing platform.
> The complexity and time consuming portion lies in the state machine.
> Your proposed state machine (TradeWhen) seems extremely simple, and
> there are already packages that perform this simple type of state
> machine (e.g., https://github.com/danielkrizian/strategery,
> https://github.com/systematicinvestor/SIT).
>
> > Rank(x)   =Rank the values of x among all instruments, and the return values
> > are float numbers equally distributed between 0.0 and 1.0
> >
> > StdDev(x, n) =Standard deviation of the values in vector x for the past n
> > days.
> >
> > Sum(x, n)= Sum of the values in vector x for the past n days.
> >
> > Correlation(x, y, n)=  Correlation of the values in vectors x and y for the
> > past n days.
> >
> > Covariance(x, y, n)  =Covariance of the values in vectors x and y for the
> > past n days.
> >
> > Count_Nans_Number(x, n)=Number of nan (Not-a-Number) values in vector x for
> > the past n days.
> >
> > Delay(x, n)-=Value of x at n days ago.
> >
> > Delta(x, n)-=x[date] - x[date - n].
> >
> > Decay_Simple_linear(x, n)
> >
> >
> > Decay_Simple_linear(x, n) = (x[date] * n + x[date - 1] * (n - 1) + ..... +
> > x[date – n - 1]) / (n + (n - 1) + … + 1)
> >
> > Ts_Rank(x, n)=Rank the values of x of the same instrument over the past n
> > days, then return the rank of the current value. The rank value is between
> > 0.0 ~ 1.0
> >
> > GroupRank(group, x)= Returns the rank of each instrument within a group,
> > which can be any matrix
> >
> > SignedPower(x, e)=Sign(x) * (Abs(x)^e)
> >
> > Ts_Skewness(x, n)=Compute the skewness of x on the last n days
> >
> > Ts_Kurtosis(x, n)=Compute the kurtosis of x on the last n days.
> >
> > Ts_Moment(x, k, n)=Compute the kth central moment of x on the last n days
> >
> > Ts_Regression(y, x, window, lag, retval)=y[t] = a + b * x[t-lag] for t in
> > (Today - window, Today)
> >
> > TradeWhen(x, y, z)=TradeWhen(triggerTradeExp, alphaExp, triggerExitExp).
> >
> > ArgMax(x, n)=Returns the relative index of the max value in the time series
> > x for the past n days.
> >
> > Ts_mean(x, n)=Calculates mean of the variable in last n days
> >
> > Ts_max(x, n)=Time series max of the value
> >
> > THESE ALL BELOW CODES PRODUCES VECTOR OF STOCK WEIGHTS FOR DIFFERENT GROUP
> > OF STOCKS
> > THESE CAN EASILY BE COMBINED WITH PERFORMANCE ANALYTICS PACKAGE FOR SHARPE
> > ,TURNOVER ,DRAWDOWN, RETURNS etc(Pnl also)
> > THESE OPERATORS WILL EASE THE WORK FOR BUILDING STRATEGIES AND CAN EASILY BE
> > EVALUATED USING PA PACKAGE IN R
> > MANY MORE OPERATORS ARE THERE.(GUI CAN ALSO BE BUILD)
> >
> > //below codes i used Fibonacci retracements and Elliot Wave Theory to find
> > the time period(n) and indicators for the reversion strategies.
> > 1.Here using volume as the filter condition and correlation between volume
> > and weighted volume price(vwap) as simple reversion strategy
> >
> > x=volume>decay_linear(volume,233);
> > y=(-1 * ts_max(rank(correlation(rank(volume), rank(vwap), 5)), 5));
> > TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
> >
> >
> > 2.Here using volume as filter condition and stochastic oscillator as the
> > base
> > reversion condition.
> >
> >
> > x=volume>sum(volume,14)/14;
> > y=-rank(((close-ts_min(low,14))/(ts_max(high,14)-ts_min(low,14)))*100);
> > TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
> >
> > 3.Using sentimental value and volume as filter condition and mean-reversion
> > strategy.
> >
> >
> > x=snt_social_value>sum(snt_social_value,14)/14 && volume>sum(volume,14)/14;
> > adv30=delay(sum(volume,30)/30,1);
> > y=-2*rank(log(close/open))+2*(( (((-1 * rank((open - delay(high, 1)))) *
> > rank((open - delay(close, 1)))) * rank((open-delay(low, 1)))))+ (-1 *
> > Ts_Rank(rank(low), 5)))+(rank(correlation(vwap, volume, 4)) <
> > rank(correlation(rank(low), rank(adv20),
> > 12)));
> > TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
> >
> > 4.Earnings per share and volume as filter condition and close-vwap
> > relationship
> >  as reversion strategy.
> >
> >
> > x=volume>sum(volume,14)/14 && eps>sum(eps,14)/14;
> > y=(vwap-close)*(close/low)^3;
> > TradeWhen(x,y,-1)
> >
> > 5.Simple reversion with no filter
> >
> > ((rank(ts_max((vwap - close), 1)) + rank(ts_min((vwap - close), 1))) *
> > rank(delta(volume, 1)))
> >
> >
> > Please other than this if there are any other project related to R and
> > finance or machine learning please tell me.(i am very interested)
> >

On Wed, 2016-09-28 at 12:38 -0700, ashwin.agr...@itbhu.ac.in
wrote:

> So can you yourself suggest some area in finance in R programming
> where i can work for the project.

There are a huge number of finance packages on CRAN.  Many are listed in
the Task View here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Finance.html

Many more are available on R-Forge or github.

I would suggest finding packages that are in your area of interest, and
working with the authors or maintainers of those packages to see where
you can add value.

Typically, the way people get involved with existing project teams is
through bug fixes, performance improvements, testing, and other
peripheral but important tasks until you are known and accepted by the
development team, at which point more access is given.

Since this is now somewhat separate from GSoC, I'll suggest that you
take further queries off-list and aim them at specific package teams.

Regards,

Brian
